_comment: Stage 2 of the staged 15B->30B pretrain (t22), Case A-prime. fb ruling 2026-08-31.
READ THIS FIRST: every epoch number in this file is measured against the STAGE-1 pool
(the packed trainable rows of the stage-1 corpus, i.e. rows of seq+1 minus the validation
holdout), NOT against the stage-2 corpus, which is not built yet. When the *_stage2 dirs
are stamped their pools will differ and every epochs value must be re-derived as
ceil(rows/pool) against the NEW pool before this file leaves _blocked.

THE WEIGHT IS THE CONTRACT, not the row columns. build_mix computes want = int(total_rows*weight) per domain, so rows_from_weight_at_runtime is what will actually be drawn; rows_table is b0's stated figure, kept for audit. They differ by a few rows per domain from independent rounding, and reviewers quoted three different math_owm counts (1,173,995 / 1,174,076 / 1,173,998) -- only the last is what runs.
Rows are the unit, not tokens. build_mix works in rows end to end and caps at
int(pool*epochs) rows; tokens are rows*4096 as a display. A token-denominated table
cannot express what the trainer does -- that is what cost stage 1 its 61,593,088-token
under-draw on cot (b0 doc section 3.1, 44 confirmed).
Stage 1 drew 3,647,072 rows = 14.9384B, not the commissioned 15.000B, because cot's
epoch cap fired. So cot has seen 5.71 RAW-SUPPLY epochs after this file's 3 more, not 6:
6.00 is measured on the pool, 5.71 on raw supply. cot epochs stay a live lever if a
math or reasoning metric reads flat at the readout (fb, 44).
KNOWN DEVIATION, pre-registered, not a bug to fix during the run: used[] restarts at 0 on
a resume (train.py:1591), so stage 2 re-reads rows stage 1 already consumed while fresh
rows sit unread -- zh_web re-reads 8% with 92% never seen, code_rp1t 58% with 26% never
seen. Every epochs figure here is a MEAN over a non-uniform pass. cot is the exception:
3 full pool epochs in each stage, so all 98,504 rows land on 6x uniformly. Fix is de-7,
seeding used[] from the checkpoint, after stage 1 ends.
Cooldown constraint (arXiv 2408.10914, fb): the 10% warmdown holds >=20% code; A-prime
carries 29%. Code stays at the 30B cumulative third (33.3%): the paper's 25% optimum is
for non-code and world knowledge, which is not this run's objective.

code_rp1t_stage2.epoch_cap_note: epochs 1 = ceil(1074096/1842469) on the STAGE-1 pool, where 1074096 is what build_mix computes as int(total_rows*weight) at runtime. The weight governs, not any row column: b0's table says 1074090 and 44 says a third figure, and the runtime value is neither. A fractional cap re-creates the stage-1 under-draw, since build_mix caps at int(pool*epochs) in ROWS.
